gates.description: Consistency model must be explicitly chosen and documented — strong, eventual, or causal with tradeoff rationale
All operations that may be retried must be idempotent — idempotency key or deduplication logic required
Partial failure modes must be enumerated and handled — no assumption that network calls either succeed fully or fail cleanly
Distributed transactions must use saga pattern with compensating transactions — no distributed 2PC
Any ordering assumption must document the clock model — wall clock ordering is not safe in distributed systems
Each identified failure mode must have an operational runbook with detection, diagnosis, and recovery steps

anti_patterns.description: Services that can only work if all of them are healthy simultaneously — distributed by deployment, monolith by coupling
Using two-phase commit for distributed transactions — blocks on coordinator failure, does not scale
Assuming a network call either fully succeeds or fully fails — real networks drop packets, split-brain is real
Using wall clock timestamps to order events across nodes — clocks drift, NTP cannot guarantee global order
Distributing a system before it has proven it needs to be distributed — adds complexity without benefit

escalation_triggers: Split-brain scenario detected in production — nodes disagree on state
Replication lag growing unbounded — follower nodes falling behind
Saga compensating transactions failing — system stuck in inconsistent state
Throughput requirements exceeding current topology capacity
Consistency guarantees violated — customers seeing stale or conflicting data
Network partition causing availability loss beyond SLA

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with consistency requirements, availability SLAs, and failure tolerance spec

output_certifications: Consistency model explicitly chosen and documented with tradeoff rationale
All retryable operations are idempotent with idempotency key or deduplication
Partial failure modes enumerated and handled
Distributed transactions use saga pattern with compensating transactions
Clock assumptions documented — no unsafe wall-clock ordering
Operational runbook exists for each identified failure mode
